trustlines.pageSubtitle: Learn how trustlines work on the Stellar network
trustlines.whatAreContent: Trustlines are explicit opt-in mechanisms on the Stellar network. They allow an account to hold and receive specific tokens issued by other accounts. Without a trustline, an account cannot receive any non-native asset.
trustlines.whyExistContent: Trustlines exist as a security feature. They prevent spam tokens from being sent to your account without your consent. This is fundamentally different from networks like Ethereum where any token can be sent to any address. On Stellar, you must explicitly trust an asset before receiving it.
trustlines.howToActivateContent: To activate a trustline, you need to submit a Change Trust operation to the Stellar network. This requires signing a transaction with your account's secret key.
trustlines.whichToTrustContent: Only trust tokens from verified issuers. Check the issuer's stellar.toml file and verify the domain. Well-known issuers include Circle (USDC, EURC) and the SDF. On testnet, the issuer for test USDC/EURC is the SDF's standard test issuer.
trustlines.reserveCostContent: Each trustline increases your account's minimum reserve by 0.5 XLM. For example, if you have 2 trustlines (USDC and EURC), you need an extra 1 XLM locked in your account. This reserve is returned when you remove the trustline.
trustlines.walletFreighterSteps:
1. Open the Freighter extension in Chrome
2. Go to Settings > Manage Assets
3. Click "Add Asset" or "Add Token"
4. Search for the asset code (e.g. USDC)
5. Select the correct issuer and confirm
6. The trustline will be added automatically
trustlines.walletLobstrSteps:
1. Open the Lobstr app on your phone
2. Go to the Assets section
3. Tap "Add Asset"
4. Search for the token (e.g. USDC)
5. Select the correct issuer from the list
6. Confirm the transaction to add the trustline
trustlines.walletLaboratorySteps:
1. Go to lab.stellar.org
2. Select "Transaction Builder"
3. Enter your public key as the source account
4. Add a "Change Trust" operation
5. Enter the asset code and issuer address
6. Sign with your secret key and submit
trustlines.removeTrustlineContent: To remove a trustline, submit a changeTrust operation with limit set to "0". Important: you must have a balance of 0 in that asset before removing the trustline. Transfer or swap all tokens first, then remove it. This will free up the 0.5 XLM reserve.
trustlines.officialDocsDescription: Learn more about trustlines and asset management in the official Stellar developer docs.
trustlines.sorobanIntro: Everything above applies to standard accounts (G... addresses). But Soroban smart contracts (C... addresses) work differently — they don't use trustlines at all.
trustlines.sorobanWhatIsSacContent: A Stellar Asset Contract (SAC) is a smart contract that wraps a classic Stellar asset (like USDC or EURC) so it can be used inside Soroban. Each classic asset has a SAC that is derived deterministically from the asset code and issuer — it's not deployed manually, the protocol generates it automatically.
trustlines.sorobanSameAsset: The key insight: a USDC that moves through a classic payment and one that moves through a SAC transfer are the same USDC. The SAC is just another gateway to the same underlying balance.
trustlines.sorobanHowReceiveContent: When someone calls the SAC's transfer(from, to, amount) function where "to" is a C... address, the SAC creates a storage entry with the contract's balance. There is no trustline check — the transfer just works.
trustlines.sorobanAntiSpamContent: Classic accounts use trustlines as anti-spam: you must opt-in before receiving tokens. Soroban takes an economic approach instead: the sender pays resource fees for creating storage entries. There is no opt-in mechanism at the protocol level — any SAC can write a balance to any contract. A contract can implement its own acceptance logic, but by default, SAC transfers always succeed.
trustlines.sorobanFaucetNote: This faucet supports both: G... addresses receive tokens via classic payments (trustline required), C... addresses receive them via SAC (no trustline needed).
trustlines.practicalExampleContent: To receive USDC on testnet: 1) Fund your account with Friendbot (10,000 XLM), 2) Add a trustline for USDC using Circle's official issuer (GBBD...LA5), 3) Request USDC from this faucet. Note: EURC uses a different issuer (GB3Q...TVO).
trustlines.summaryWhatBrief: Trustlines let your Stellar account hold non-native tokens like USDC and EURC. Without one, you can't receive these assets.
trustlines.summaryWhy: Why do I need one for USDC/EURC?
trustlines.summaryWhyBrief: Stellar requires explicit opt-in before receiving tokens. This protects you from unwanted spam tokens. Add a trustline to start receiving stablecoins.

apiDocs.title: API Reference
apiDocs.subtitle: Public endpoints for programmatic access to the faucet
apiDocs.rateLimitDescription: All endpoints are rate limited per IP and per address. When exceeded, a 429 response is returned with X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining, and X-RateLimit-Reset headers.
apiDocs.webhookDescription: Pass an optional callbackUrl (HTTPS, public) in your request body. After funding completes, a POST with the result payload will be sent to your URL (fire-and-forget, 5s timeout).
